images.title: One array or two
images.purpose: Show that 19 tiles make only one array, 1 × 19, so only two factors, while 21 tiles make two arrays, 1 × 21 and 3 × 7, so four factors.
images.composition: Two columns: one row of 19 tiles on the left with only two factors, and two arrays of 21 tiles on the right with four factors.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two columns. LEFT, headed 19 tiles (centred at x 400 and y 70, bold dark #1F2937, 48 px): exactly 1 row of 19 square tiles, every tile 30 by 30 px filled teal #0072B2 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and 4 px between tiles, x 80 to 722 and y 260 to 290; under the row, centred at x 400 and y 350, the text 1 × 19 = 19 (44 px bold), and under that, centred at x 400 and y 420, the text only two factors: 1 and 19 (40 px). RIGHT, headed 21 tiles (centred at x 1060 and y 70, bold dark, 48 px): ARRAY A, 3 rows of 7 tiles (21 tiles), every tile 44 by 44 px filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark outline and 6 px between tiles, x 800 to 1144 and y 130 to 274, with the text 3 × 7 = 21 to its right, left aligned at x 1170 and y 202 (40 px bold); ARRAY B, 1 row of 21 tiles, every tile 22 by 22 px filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with a thin dark outline and 4 px between tiles, x 800 to 1342 and y 360 to 382, with the text 1 × 21 = 21 under it, left aligned at x 800 and y 420 (40 px bold). Under both arrays, centred at x 1060 and y 520, the text four factors: 1, 3, 7, 21 (40 px bold). In all 61 tiles. A thin vertical grey #6B7280 line at x 760 from y 120 to y 560 separates the columns. No other text and no numbers inside the tiles. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A number with only one array has only two factors, 1 and itself, and is a prime number.
images.description: One row of 19 tiles as the only array of 19, beside the two arrays of 21 tiles, 3 × 7 and 1 × 21.
images.context: Concept image for Numbers With Only Two Factors. It follows the idea of the arrays for 13 and 37 in your maths book (a number with only one array) and uses this concept's own example, 19 and 21.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how many arrays each number can make before showing the factors. The slip to watch is saying a number with one array has no factors.

image_decisions.why: Seeing 19 tiles with one array next to 21 tiles with two makes 'only two factors' countable.
